text:
maria_support: customer reports 401 invalid_api_key when hitting /v1/generate after a deploy. They say the key "looks like a long JWT" and was pulled from Secret Manager during CI.
ryan_eng: can you paste the failing curl (sanitized)?
maria_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6...\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` 
maria_support: error: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid or expired API key"}
tom_sre: that header looks like a Google signed JWT (3 parts with dots). Redwood API keys are opaque single-token strings, not signed JWTs. Looks like CI stored the service-account signed JWT instead of the Redwood key.
ryan_eng: +1 — quick check: tokens with two dots (.) are almost always JWTs. We should confirm what was written to Secret Manager. maria, can you run `gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=my-app/redwood_key` on the instance or show CI step? (sanitized output is fine)
maria_support: CI step (sanitized): `gcloud iam service-accounts sign-jwt --iam-account=sa@app.iam.gserviceaccount.com payload.json > /tmp/key.jwt` then `gcloud secrets versions add redwood_key --data-file=/tmp/key.jwt`
ryan_eng: yep that's the culprit — the pipeline is generating and storing a signed JWT. The app later reads redwood_key and sends it as Authorization Bearer, which Redwood rejects (401).
ryan_eng: remediation: 1) rotate the Redwood API key from Console (create new key, revoke old) 2) update CI to fetch the plaintext Redwood key (or use Secret Manager to store the real key) instead of generating a signed JWT 3) add a validation test to CI that does a lightweight /v1/health call and fails early if 401.
maria_support: suggested quick guard for infra: reject secrets with two dots via a pre-check in the deploy pipeline (regex to detect JWT pattern) — we can add that as a stopgap.
deploy-bot: Deployment failed: integration-tests (branch: main) — failed healthcheck: 401 invalid_api_key
tom_sre: I advised customer to rotate key and update pipeline. They rotated, replaced secret with the new API key, redeployed and confirmed: curl now returns 200.
maria_support: customer confirmed issue resolved. Action items: add CI pre-check for tokens, update docs snippet to show correct API key storage, and file a runbook entry under eng-infra for this misconfiguration.
ryan_eng: filing follow-up ticket with infra to add the regex gate and a note in onboarding docs.
maria_support: closing thread after customer ack.
